author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthCold Weather Could Predict an Increase in Heart Attacks Three Days in AdvanceAnd the holidays are especially bad JCBy Jake Currie4:00 PM CDT on September 16, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHumans have done a great job of building artificial infrastructure to insulate ourselves from the natural world—cities, homes, air conditioning, etc. We’re so good at constructing comfort-maximizing bubbles that it’s easy to forget we’re still very much at the mercy of Mother Nature, in big ways and small. For example, a new study published in Public Health recently found that even the incidence of heart attacks may be under the sway of the weather.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Looking at the 4 Oldest Galaxies Ever Discovered!ShareNextStayCardiovascular diseases have long been known to peak during the colder months in both the northern and southern hemispheres. In fact, the holidays can be a particularly deadly time for heart attacks here in the United States. To tease apart the different potential contributing factors, a team of Hungarian cardiac specialists compared data on cardiac arrests with meteorological measures like temperature, wind speed, atmospheric pressure, and more. Altogether, their dataset included more than 114,000 out-of-hospital heart attack cases in Hungary between November 2018 and December 2023. Read more: “Night Owls Could Be Putting Their Heart Health at Risk”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
